title: Гость всегда прав  (The Guest Is Always Right)

segments.t: In the kitchen, Vika tries to persuade Chef Barinov to humor the guest and fry the steak tartare, reminding him that the customer is always right. Meanwhile, Max tells Kostya about waking up in a panic beside Sasha and admits he is relieved thinking she has flown off to Cyprus for a few days.
Ой, какая трагедия.
Ведь тебе что, сложно?
Ты же знаешь, гость всегда прав.
На моей кухне я всегда прав.
Разговор окончен.
Просыпаюсь я с Сашей.
Я чуть с ума не сошел.
Слушай, но клоуну намного страшнее.
И вообще.
Слава богу, Саша на Кипр улетела.
Пару дней можно об этом не думать.
А потом выбери.
Все равно рано или поздно придется.
Right, let's take their exchange slowly and unpack the Russian.
Ой, какая трагедия.
'Oh, what a tragedy.' The meaning hinges on 'oh no' working together with 'a tragedy' in spoken Russian.
Ведь тебе что, сложно?
'Is it really that hard for you?' The grammar packs 'you know' and 'difficult' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Ты же знаешь, гость всегда прав.
'You know that the guest is always right.' Vika addresses the listener with the informal singular 'you' alongside 'right'. Sasha answers right away.
На моей кухне я всегда прав.
'In my kitchen, I am always right.' In Russian, the idea of 'on' flows naturally into 'right' without extra filler words.
Разговор окончен.
'This conversation is over.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'conversation' before landing on 'is finished'.
Просыпаюсь я с Сашей.
'I wake up next to Sasha.' Notice how Russian expresses 'to wake up' and 'Sasha' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Vika answers right away.
Я чуть с ума не сошел.
'I nearly lost my mind.' Vika anchors the line on 'I', while 'stepped off' completes the thought.
Слушай, но клоуну намного страшнее.
'Listen, clowns are way scarier though.' Sasha brings out the contrast between 'listen' and 'but' in a few short words.
И вообще.
'And besides.' The meaning hinges on 'both' working together with 'at all' in spoken Russian. Sasha answers right away.
Слава богу, Саша на Кипр улетела.
'Thank goodness Sasha flew off to Cyprus.' The meaning hinges on 'glory' working together with 'to fly away' in spoken Russian.
Пару дней можно об этом не думать.
'For a couple of days I do not have to think about it.' Vika anchors the line on 'couple', while 'to think' completes the thought.
А потом выбери.
'And after that, make your choice.' In Russian, the idea of 'and' flows naturally into 'to choose' without extra filler words. Vika answers right away.
Все равно рано или поздно придется.

'Sooner or later you will have to anyway.' The grammar packs 'all' and 'it will be necessary' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Now let's listen to the entire scene again without interruption.
